name: Lopa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. Comparative Kainji: main text [The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria]. Circulation draft, 11 May 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Section 3.2 Lake (pp. 8-9) gives ethnonyms, villages and subgrouping for Rop/Rerang with tone-marked forms (e.g. [dɔ̀ɾóp], [òːɾɔ́p], [òlːɔ́p]); section 4.2.2 'Rop' under 4 Phonology (p. 31) is an empty heading in this draft. The word 'stress' does not occur in the document; tone is discussed only for Cinda and Hungwəryə. Footnote 3 (p. 8) dismisses Adekunle (1986) as not describing Lopa.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. 'The Lake languages' web page, rogerblench.info (Wayback 2015-04-20)
sources.note: Index page only: 'three languages, Rop, Shen and Shuba'; no linked documents, nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Lopa language of Northwestern Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 2 June 2006. Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 27 pp. (Glottolog ref 16298, hhtype wordlist)
sources.note: Section 3 Phonology (pp. 2-3) covers vowels, consonants and '3.3 Tones: Tone on verb stems tends to be predictable as with many Kambari lects.' (p. 3); p. 1 says 'In general, tones are not marked'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 27 pp. Wordlist collected at Tsupamini, 26 Nov 1992, in a 'one-shot' session; phonology 'tentative'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page lopa1238 and reference records 16298, 66310; Wikipedia 'Lopa language'; ISO 639-3 page for lop
sources.note: Used only to locate sources. Glottolog lists 3 refs (Bertho 1952, Gunn & Conant 1960, Blench 2006) plus Blench n.d.; Wikipedia adds Blench 2012 overview and McGill 2012 MS. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. [2012-2025 versions]. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria / Comparative Kainji. Cambridge: KWEF. Current version on rogerblench.info (site behind SiteGround captcha; only the 11 May 2012 draft was reachable via Wayback)

sources.citation: Adekunle, [initials unknown]. 1986. [Phonology sketch of Lopa; probably a Nigerian university BA/MA thesis; full reference absent from Blench 2006 and Blench & McGill 2012 bibliographies]
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only work anyone has called a phonology of Lopa; a phonology sketch is the most likely place for a stress/tone statement. Caveat: Blench compared its lexicon with two independent Lopa wordlists and found almost no resemblance, so it may describe a different language.
